# E2E flow command reference

How to write and check flows: [e2e-flows.md](e2e-flows.md). Every command's mapping form also takes `when` and `timeout`.

- **Short form**: `bare` means the command can stand alone (`- launchApp`); `value → key` means `- cmd: value` is `- cmd: { key: value }`.
- **Keys**: `*` = required. `any selector` = the selector keys (`id`, `role`, `label`, `text`, `within`, `index`, `window`, `below`, `above`, `leftOf`, `rightOf`, `point`); a bare string is visible text.
- **driver**: needs the Spark in-app driver (white-box). Everything else is black-box (OS input + accessibility tree).
- **runner**: the runner runs it over the build on disk, with no backend.
- **maestro**: Maestro core command; keeps Maestro semantics.

## Lifecycle

| Command | Short form | Keys | Backend | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `launchApp` | bare | `appId`, `clearState`, `stopApp`, `arguments`, `env`, `openFile`, `openUrl`, `from` | black-box, maestro | Launch the app. Restarts it first when running unless stopApp is false. |
| `launchSecondInstance` | bare | `arguments`, `env`, `openFile`, `openUrl` | black-box | Launch a second instance; pair with assertSingleInstance. |
| `assertSingleInstance` | bare | — | black-box | Assert exactly one app process is running. |
| `stopApp` | bare | — | black-box, maestro | Stop the app. |
| `preserveAppDefaults` | value → `keys` | `keys`* | driver | Before launchApp: snapshot these keys of the app's defaults and restore them when the flow ends, even after a failure or timeout. Refuses while the app runs. |
| `killApp` | bare | — | black-box, maestro | Kill the app process. |
| `quitApp` | bare | `via` | black-box | Quit the app the way a user would. |
| `crashApp` | value → `kind` | `kind`* | black-box | Crash the app. |
| `assertCrashRecovery` | bare | — | black-box | Assert the app recovers after crashApp. |
| `relaunchApp` | bare | `preserveState` | black-box | Quit and relaunch the app. |
| `assertAppState` | — | `running`, `active`, `hidden`, `dockIconVisible` (at least one) | black-box | Assert process and activation state. |
| `assertStartup` | — | `coldMs`, `firstPaintMs`, `id`; at least one of `coldMs`, `firstPaintMs` | driver | Assert startup phase timings in milliseconds. With `id`, coldMs ends when the element with that testID first shows in a settled UI. |

State fields go with their event type and override what getSystemInfo, getNetworkStatus and getAppearancePreferences report until the app quits: thermal (thermalChanged), lowPower (lowPowerChanged), source (powerChanged), network (networkChanged), appearance and automaticAppearance (appearanceChanged), accentColor and highlightColor (systemColorsChanged), increaseContrast, reduceTransparency, reduceMotion, differentiateWithoutColor and invertColors (accessibilityDisplayChanged); memoryPressure needs level. |
| `simulatePermission` | — | `kind`*, `authorization`, `answer`; at least one of `authorization`, `answer` | driver | Set the simulated state @legendapp/spark/permissions reports for a kind, in-process: its macOS authorization and the answer its simulated prompt gets (ignore: it never answers; null clears the answer). Never reaches TCC; the permission command changes the OS. |
| `assertSimulatedPermission` | — | `kind`*, `authorization`, `requests`, `prompts`, `settingsOpened`; at least one of `authorization`, `requests`, `prompts`, `settingsOpened` | driver | Assert a kind's simulated permission state: its authorization, and how many requests reached it, prompts it showed and times its System Settings pane was opened (never really opened). |
| `simulateBiometrics` | — | `biometryType`, `biometrics`, `password`, `answer`, `enrollmentChanged` (at least one) | driver | Set the simulated state @legendapp/spark/biometrics reports, in-process: the sensor, whether biometrics alone and biometrics or the login password can be evaluated, and how the next simulated prompts end (ignore: they stay up until cancelled; null clears the answer, so prompts reject E_UNAVAILABLE). enrollmentChanged: true removes biometryCurrentSet secrets, as adding or removing a fingerprint does. Never shows a Touch ID or password prompt or touches a keychain. |
| `assertSimulatedBiometrics` | — | `prompts`, `pending`, `lastOperation`, `lastReason`, `lastFallback`, `secrets` (at least one) | driver | Assert the simulated biometric state: how many prompts were shown, how many are still up, the last prompt's operation (authenticate or secret), reason and fallback, and the stored secrets with their access (exactly). |
| `simulateAuthorization` | — | `appleId`, `webCredentials`, `answer`, `credentialState` (at least one) | driver | Set the simulated state @legendapp/spark/apple-authentication and /passkeys report, in-process: whether the app has the Sign in with Apple entitlement and webcredentials for which domains (the simulation starts from the build's real entitlements), how the next requests end (success, cancel, a failure reason, or ignore: they stay up until cancelled; null clears the answer, so requests reject E_UNAVAILABLE), and the Apple ID credential state (null: signed-in users authorized, others notFound). Never presents a sheet or reaches Apple or a relying party. |
| `assertSimulatedAuthorization` | — | `requests`, `pending`, `lastOperation`, `lastWindow`, `lastRelyingPartyId`, `passkeys` (at least one) | driver | Assert the simulated authorization state: how many requests were shown, how many are still up, the last request's operation (appleId, createPasskey or getPasskey), the window it was presented over and its relying party, and how many simulated passkeys exist. |
| `simulatePrivilegedHelper` | — | `signed`, `helpers`, `approval`, `promptAnswer`, `connection`, `expireAuthorizations` (at least one) | driver | Set the simulated state @legendapp/spark/privileged-helper reports, in-process: whether the app is signed by a team (the simulation starts from the build's real signature), each named helper's launchd status (unset helpers are notFound unless the build embeds their plist), whether registering needs the person's approval (required: requiresApproval; granted: enabled), how the next admin prompts end (null: they reject E_UNAVAILABLE) and how the simulated helper's connection behaves (accept: it echoes the message; invalid: it refuses the connection; interrupted: it exits mid-request); expireAuthorizations: true lapses every held admin authorization, as the right's timeout does. Never calls SMAppService, shows an admin prompt, reaches launchd or runs anything as root. |
| `assertSimulatedPrivilegedHelper` | — | `registrations`, `unregistrations`, `settingsOpened`, `prompts`, `lastPrompt`, `authorizations`, `messages`, `lastHelper`, `lastAuthorized`, `helpers` (at least one) | driver | Assert what the @legendapp/spark/privileged-helper simulation recorded: registrations and unregistrations that reached it, times Login Items settings were opened (never really opened), admin prompts shown and the last prompt's text, admin authorizations held, messages sent, the last message's helper and whether admin rights came with it, and helper statuses (each listed one exactly). |
| `simulateSharing` | — | `shareAnswer`, `services`, `invokeService`, `openSpotlightItem`, `openUniversalLink` (at least one) | driver | Drive the in-process simulation of @legendapp/spark/sharing: how the simulated share picker answers (a service title, or dismiss; null makes share reject), the services the app's Info.plist would declare, a run of a registered service as the Services menu would (text on a private pasteboard), and opening a Spotlight item or an https universal link through the app delegate as macOS does. Never shows a picker, writes the Spotlight index or reaches pbs. |
| `assertSharing` | — | `shares`, `lastShare`, `indexed`, `registered`, `invocations` (at least one) | driver | Assert what the @legendapp/spark/sharing simulation recorded: the number of shares, the last share (its items, whether it had an anchor view, the service it got), the ids in the simulated Spotlight index (sorted), the services with a listener, and the number of service invocations. |
| `simulateSpeech` | — | `wordMs`, `recognizerAvailable`, `onDeviceSupported`, `recognitionPartials`, `recognitionTranscript` (at least one) | driver | Set the simulated state @legendapp/spark/speech reports, in-process: how long a simulated word takes (wordMs), whether the recognizer is available and recognizes on device, the partial transcripts a recognition reports while listening (one per word time) and its final transcript once stopped (null: nobody spoke). Never speaks aloud, listens to a microphone or reaches a recognizer or TCC. |
| `assertSimulatedSpeech` | — | `utterances`, `lastText`, `lastVoice`, `lastRate`, `lastPitch`, `lastVolume`, `speaking`, `paused`, `recognitions`, `listening`, `lastLocale`, `lastOnDevice` (at least one) | driver | Assert the simulated speech state: how many utterances were spoken (recorded, never heard) and the last one's text, voice, rate, pitch and volume; whether speech is speaking or paused; how many recognitions ran, whether one is listening, and the last one's locale and onDevice option. |
| `simulateAppIntents` | — | `intents`, `invoke` (at least one) | driver | Drive the in-process simulation of @legendapp/spark/app-intents: the intents the app's macos.appIntents would declare (replacing the previous ones), and an invocation of one as Shortcuts, Spotlight or Siri would run it, with its parameters and how long it waits for an answer (default 30 s). Never reaches the system: nothing is donated or registered with Shortcuts. |
| `assertAppIntents` | — | `registered`, `invocations`, `pending`, `lastInvocation`, `donations`, `lastDonation` (at least one) | driver | Assert what the @legendapp/spark/app-intents simulation recorded: the intents with a handler (sorted), how many invocations completed and how many still wait, the last completed invocation (its id, parameters, the text it returned, or its error code; null for none), and the number of donations and the last one. |
| `simulateCapture` | — | `cameras`, `microphones`, `cameraEntitled`, `microphoneEntitled` (at least one) | driver | Set the simulated capture devices @legendapp/spark/capture sees, in-process: whether the simulated camera and microphone are connected, and whether the build has the camera and microphone entitlements (cameraEntitled, microphoneEntitled; default the build's real state, missing in a hardened-runtime build without macos.capture). Disconnecting one ends its running session with E_UNAVAILABLE, as unplugging it would. Never opens a camera, microphone or ScreenCaptureKit, or reaches TCC. |
| `assertSimulatedCapture` | — | `cameras`, `microphones`, `recordingAudio`, `cameraRunning`, `recordingScreen`, `photos`, `screenshots`, `recordings`, `minFrames`, `minLevels` (at least one) | driver | Assert the simulated capture state: which simulated devices are connected, which sessions run (an audio recording, the camera, a screen recording), how many photos, screenshots and finished recordings they produced, and at least how many synthetic camera or screen frames and microphone levels flowed. |
| `permission` | — | `grant`, `revoke`, `reset` (exactly one) | black-box | Grant, revoke or reset a privacy permission. |
| `setFocusMode` | value → `mode` | `mode`* | black-box | Set the OS Focus mode. |

| `assertFormatted` | — | `id`*, `equals`* | black-box | Assert locale-formatted text. |

| `assertIdleCpu` | — | `for`*, `maxPercent`* | driver | Assert CPU use while idle. |
| `assertNoLeaks` | — | `since`, `repeat`, `run`; at least one of `since`, `run` | driver | Assert leak counters (windows, views, listeners, native handles) return to baseline. |

| `stopTrace` | value → `name` | `name`* | driver | Stop and save the trace. |

## State introspection

| Command | Short form | Keys | Backend | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assertState` | — | `path`*, `equals`* | driver | Assert app state by path. |
| `assertCrashSymbol` | — | `path`*, `symbol`* | driver | Assert the native crash report at state `path` has a frame named `symbol`. A dev build's report carries in-process names; a release build is stripped, so the report is symbolicated with the dSYMs in the `dSYMs` folder next to the app (as `spark symbolicate`), and a release build without them fails. |

## Security audits

| Command | Short form | Keys | Backend | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assertSandboxVariant` | value → `app` | `app`* | runner | Assert the App Sandbox (Mac App Store) variant leaves out what a sandboxed app cannot use: no Sparkle code or SU* Info.plist keys, and no launch daemons (privileged helpers) in Contents/Library/LaunchDaemons. |
| `assertEntitlements` | — | `app`*, `sandbox`*, `allow` | runner | Assert every process of the app is signed with only the entitlements `allow` names, each with its reason, and never get-task-allow; an `allow` entry no process carries fails. `sandbox`: whether this is the sandboxed variant, which sandboxes every process. |
| `assertCodeSigning` | value → `app` | `app`* | runner | Assert every Mach-O file of the app is signed by the main executable's team (not ad-hoc), every process has the hardened runtime, and none disables library validation. |
| `assertNoDebugSurface` | bare | `for` | driver | Relaunch the app pointed at a decoy development server (RCT_jsLocation and SPARK_BUNDLE_URL) and, once its first UI settles and `for` (default 2s) more, assert it never connected to it, holds no network socket and no bound Unix socket but the driver's (lsof), has no Developer menu or debug menu item (DevTools, inspector, debugger, profiler), hidden ones included, and that no JavaScript in the app contains the network inspector or the profiler and no native code contains the profiler. For release builds. |
| `assertLoadPaths` | value → `app` | `app`* | runner | Assert no load path lets a library from outside the bundle or the system into the app: LC_RPATH entries, dependencies (weak ones too) and LC_DYLD_ENVIRONMENT. On Windows: the DLL search order, not implemented yet (#51). |

## Build audits

| Command | Short form | Keys | Backend | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `assertAppIcon` | value → `app` | `app`*, `styles` | runner | Assert the app's icon has every size the platform draws: on macOS 32 to 1024 px asset catalog renditions and a valid .icns, on Windows the executable's 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64 and 256 px icons. `styles`: the macOS 26 Icon Composer styles it must carry (default, dark, clear, tinted). |

## Manual steps

| Command | Short form | Keys | Backend | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `manualStep` | — | `instruction`*, `expect`*, `evidence`, `screenshot`, `signoff` | black-box | A step a person checks and signs off. The runner records it as awaiting sign-off and runs on; `bun run gate:signoff` collects the sign-off. `screenshot` names the earlier takeScreenshot that shows what to check (`evidence: screenshot` needs one); with no screenshot, a pass needs a note. Only in `manual: partial` or `manual: true` flows. |
